chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
"Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ruled concerning
the dāmiyah: one camel; the bāḍiʿah: two camels; the mutalāḥimah: three camels; and the simḥāq: four camels."

key_terms.أَبْعِرَةٍ: camels, the unit of compensation in diyah
key_terms.السِّمْحَاقِ: a wound reaching the thin membrane over the bone
key_terms.الْبَاضِعَةِ: a wound that cuts into the flesh
key_terms.الْمُتَلَاحِمَةِ: a deeper flesh wound penetrating further into tissue

ai.seo_question: What are the diyah amounts for different types of shijāj wounds in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives specific legal rulings for blood-money compensation for different categories of head and facial wounds. It attributes these fixed amounts to the judgment of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, showing graded compensation according to the severity of the injury.
